what: Nu Holdings runs Nubank, the largest digital bank in Latin America. It serves about 120 million customers in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia with credit cards, accounts, loans and investments, entirely through an app and without branches.
customers: Consumers and small businesses in Brazil above all, plus a fast-growing base in Mexico and Colombia.
money: interest and fees on cards, personal loans and payroll loans
interest earned on deposits, plus investments, insurance and marketplace fees
moat: The lowest cost to serve a customer in the region because it has no branches, combined with a brand that acquires customers largely by word of mouth.
risks: Brazilian interest rates and unemployment drive credit losses
Reported revenue fell about 8% last year on currency and rate effects
Expansion into Mexico and Colombia is expensive before it becomes profitable
Brazilian regulators are tightening rules on card interest and fees
opportunities: It serves a population where tens of millions were previously unbanked
Deposits fund lending cheaply, which is the key advantage over fintech rivals
Mexico is growing fast and could become a second large market
watch: Customer growth outside Brazil and the non-performing loan ratio.
